# v0.21 natural target-priority measurement

Scope: deterministic **engine-earned** profiles, not browser-earned acceptance. No edited stats, granted items, forced combat RNG, enemy tuning, or hidden live-game manipulation. Synthetic correctness fixtures belong in separate tests.

## Reproduce

From `dot-game/`: `node scripts/measure-target-priority.mjs > target-priority-results.json`.

The standalone script uses only this checkpoint's own engine/loot modules. It prints every cohort row and all measured metrics. JSON output SHA256 for this run: `2678d65627f2f6ae1e6be6e6ec72dec881fe3a264ee03e525388d36bdd0d41f7`.

## Predeclared acquisition and comparisons

- Seeds1–20,12 normal acquisition expeditions each, choosing the highest unlocked route up to8. If an acquisition failed, the next attempt would farm one route lower; no failure occurred. The25-run bound and unlock check were established before running.
- Equip owned gear with the existing score heuristic between expeditions; learn/slot the three rank1 ability lines when ordinarily eligible. This heuristic is a reproducible acquisition protocol, not a player-facing best-build recommendation.
- 240 acquisition wins, zero defeats; all earned profiles were Lv11 and had unlocked route9. Each cloned profile legally purchases and equips axe/Slaughter, club/Slaughter or rapier/Nimble using earned credits. No free commission or forced item quality.
- Routes5,6,7,8 × three commission families ×20 seeds = **240 triples /720 test expeditions**. Every triple begins with identical earned gear, stats, saved RNG and resources; only the camp-selected policy differs. All720 won.
- Routes5–6 are useful controls: their caster is first or alone. Routes7–8 include a caster behind another enemy. No route was changed to make a policy look good.

## Results compared with default 依序集火

| Policy | HP loss lower / equal / higher | Faster / equal / slower | Fewer / same / more magic casts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 施法者優先 | 69 /129 /42 | 33 /170 /37 | 94 /146 /0 |
| 低血量收尾 | 6 /229 /5 | 5 /234 /1 | 3 /237 /0 |

Caster-first's120 route5–6 rows are identical on measured metrics. On routes7–8 alone it lowers HP loss69 times, leaves it equal9 times and raises it42 times. There is no universal survival/speed advantage: all policies won in this bounded cohort, so no win-rate improvement was established.

- Seed1, axe, stage7: caster-first changes HP loss345→333 but time20.0→22.1s; casts1→0. Less damage does not imply a faster clear.
- Seed1, axe, stage8: caster-first changes HP loss380→393 and time21.0→19.5s; casts1→0. Preventing a cast does not prove lower total HP loss. Lowest-HP produces the same changed result here.
- Seed9, rapier/Nimble, stage6: lowest-HP changes HP loss174→156 at the same16.8s, with zero magic casts in either run. The policy can matter through naturally distributed damage even without a caster-order difference.

Changed targets change downstream combat checks and RNG consumption; these are whole-expedition paired observations, not isolated causal estimates of one damage formula. The mostly equal lowest-HP results reflect naturally focused attacks; the feature is not tuned to manufacture a large advantage. This cohort is not late-game balance, defeat-recovery, offline or mobile validation.

## Retained rows

All rows are wins and level11. Compact cells are `HP loss / seconds / magic casts / min HP% / counters / MP spent / target changes`; min HP% is rounded only in this table. The script output retains full precision, initial saved RNG and owned weapon ID. Target changes count changes between non-null live target IDs across the expedition, including wave changes; they are not a pure within-wave switching count.
